paragraphs: On Saturday, Grandpa takes Tom and Lily to the café on the town street. Pip waits under the table. They sit at a small table by the window. The children are thirsty. "Excuse me, please," says Grandpa, "three glasses of juice." Then he looks at the menu. "I like fish," he says. "The fish here is delicious."

"Do you like fish, Tom?" asks Lily. "No, I don't," says Tom. "Why not?" asks Grandpa. "Because it is terrible," says Tom. "It has a lot of bones!" Lily laughs. Tom says no to the fish, and Lily watches him. "I like fish, but I like salad more," she says. "I like the taste of carrots." "I don't like vegetables," says Tom. Grandpa smiles. "And I don't like salad," he says.

"Then what can we eat?" asks Grandpa. Tom looks at the menu again. "Pasta!" he says. They share a big plate of pasta with a red sauce. Tom eats a lot of pasta, and he smiles. The pasta is hot and soft, and the sauce is sweet. "Do you like it?" asks Grandpa. "Yes, I do!" says Tom. "Me too!" says Lily. Lily takes some pasta on her fork. Pip puts his nose up, and Lily gives him a bit of pasta. At the end, Grandpa pays. Grandpa takes a photo of the happy table. "Thank you, Grandpa," says Tom. Grandpa looks at the children and laughs. Everybody is happy.
text.summary: Grandpa takes Tom and Lily to a café. Tom does not like fish, and Grandpa does not like salad, so they share a plate of pasta.
